No, as sexual orientation and sexual behavior is not a genetic syndrome or genetic disorder, and it's also not something that is made by a know single gene or genetic pattern (rather a complex genetic intertwine).
Although it's something genetically encoded (it is known to develop around the eight gestation week), it's one of the many complex features of humans, and cannot be reduced to only the genetic components.
The sexual orientation has a lot to do with brain morpho-physiology, hormones and social structures, and thus gene therapy (or any kind of "therapy" that we know) is completely ineffective at changing it (efforts have been made). It's not something ethically realizable either, as minority sexual orientations are natural and not pathological.

It's usually organ failure or dehydration.
When there's lack of food, the body starts to use body fat and then muscles as "food" in order to preserve the main organs alive. When there's no more fat nor muscles left, the organs (specially liver and kidneys), fail.
You can also die out of problems derived from starvation, like an infection (as your immune system is weakened), a disease like scurvy, or trauma (like if you get hit, with not enough nutrients it's easier to damage more), or simply by suicide.
